peptide.name: Tesamorelin
peptide.summary: Tesamorelin is an FDA-approved synthetic analog of the full 44-amino-acid growth-hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH), marketed as Egrifta. It is approved specifically to reduce excess visceral abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. Unlike exogenous growth hormone, it stimulates the pituitary's own pulsatile GH release via the GHRH receptor.
peptide.description: Tesamorelin is GHRH(1-44) modified with a trans-3-hexenoic acid group at the N-terminal tyrosine, which confers resistance to DPP-IV enzymatic degradation and extends its short native half-life. It was FDA-approved in November 2010 (Egrifta) for reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-positive adults with lipodystrophy, based on a pivotal phase III trial (Falutz et al., NEJM 2007, n=412) showing a 15.2% reduction in visceral adipose tissue, an 81% increase in IGF-1, and improvements in triglycerides and cholesterol ratio at 26 weeks. Newer formulations (Egrifta SV, approved 2019; Egrifta WR) reduce injection volume and reconstitution frequency but are not interchangeable milligram-for-milligram with the original formulation. It selectively reduces visceral fat with little effect on subcutaneous fat or body weight, and its effect reverses if treatment is stopped.
peptide.mechanism_of_action: Binds the GHRH receptor (GHRHR) on pituitary somatotrophs, activating the Gs-alpha/adenylate cyclase/cAMP pathway to stimulate pulsatile GH synthesis and release. This raises hepatic IGF-1 production, which drives preferential lipolysis of visceral adipose tissue.

half_life.note: Elimination half-life approximately 26-38 minutes; the N-terminal modification extends this relative to native GHRH but daily dosing is still required.

peptide.evidence_note: Approved based on a pivotal randomized controlled trial (n=412) and confirmed by later randomized trials showing reduced visceral adipose tissue and liver fat versus placebo. Extensive safety data over 12+ months of continuous treatment.
peptide.fda_status_note: FDA-approved (Egrifta, November 2010; Egrifta SV, 2019; Egrifta WR) specifically for reduction of excess abdominal fat in HIV-infected adults with lipodystrophy. Not approved or recommended for general weight loss. Prescription-only.
peptide.compounding_note: An FDA-approved drug. The different approved formulations (Egrifta, Egrifta SV, Egrifta WR) are not interchangeable milligram-for-milligram per the FDA label.

benefits.label: Reduces visceral adipose tissue
benefits.detail: Pivotal trial showed -15.2% visceral fat versus placebo at 26 weeks; later RCT found a net VAT treatment effect of about -42 cm2.

benefits.label: Raises IGF-1
benefits.detail: 81% increase in IGF-1 in pivotal trial, reflecting sustained physiologic GH stimulation.

benefits.label: Improves lipid parameters
benefits.detail: Reduced triglycerides (~-50 mg/dL) and improved cholesterol/HDL ratio in the pivotal trial.

benefits.label: Reduced liver fat (secondary)
benefits.detail: A later RCT found a net -2.9% reduction in liver fat versus placebo.

risks.label: Fluid retention / edema
risks.detail: GH-axis stimulation can cause peripheral edema and arthralgia.

risks.label: Elevated IGF-1 (long-term unknown)
risks.detail: Effects of prolonged IGF-1 elevation are not fully characterized; monitor levels during treatment.

risks.label: Effect reverses on discontinuation
risks.detail: Visceral fat reduction is not durable after stopping treatment.

contraindications.label: Active or suspected malignancy
contraindications.detail: Discontinue if there is evidence of recurrent malignancy; GH stimulation is a theoretical concern.

contraindications.label: Pituitary disease / prior pituitary surgery or radiation

interactions.effect: GH-axis stimulation may affect glucose regulation; monitor.

reconstitution.note: Supplied as a lyophilized powder reconstituted with the provided Sterile Water for Injection. Egrifta SV: 1.4 mg (0.35 mL) daily. Egrifta WR: 1.28 mg daily, vial sufficient for 7 doses, reconstituted weekly. Original Egrifta: 2 mg SC once daily. Formulations are NOT interchangeable mg-for-mg; follow the specific product's reconstitution instructions.

lyophilized.tempC: room temperature or refrigerate per product
lyophilized.stability: Per FDA label for each formulation.

reconstituted.stability: Use within the product-specific window; Egrifta WR extends usable window to about a week.

peptide.disclaimer: For research and educational purposes only. This is not medical advice. Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is a prescription drug approved for a specific indication; use only under a licensed healthcare provider.

dose_ranges.context: HIV-associated lipodystrophy, visceral fat reduction (approved labeling, Egrifta SV)
dose_ranges.note: Egrifta SV approved dose is 1.4 mg (0.35 mL reconstituted) SC once daily into the abdomen, rotating sites. Original Egrifta is 2 mg SC once daily; Egrifta WR is 1.28 mg once daily (weekly reconstitution). Formulations are not interchangeable. Follow the specific product's prescribing information.

protocols.name: Visceral fat reduction (per FDA label)
protocols.description: Approved labeling specifies once-daily subcutaneous dosing into the abdomen with site rotation. Trials demonstrating visceral-fat reduction ran 26-52 weeks; effect reverses upon discontinuation. Summarized from approved labeling and trial designs.
protocols.cycling_notes: Chronic therapy while indication persists; managed by a prescriber. Not cycled.
protocols.disclaimer: Summary of approved labeling for educational reference. Not a substitute for the prescribing information or medical advice.

related.note: Both are GHRH-receptor analogs, though tesamorelin is the full GHRH(1-44) sequence with an approved clinical indication, while CJC-1295 (no DAC) is a shorter GHRH(1-29) fragment sold as a research chemical.
